theoremCandidate.traceCohomology: In the physical BRST quotient, write [T]=c_H[O_H]+sum_I b_I[X_I], where b_I are convention-matched beta/anomalous coefficients and X_I are renormalized gauge-invariant scalar operators.
theoremCandidate.stateIdentity: For a physical state n with F_H^n nonzero, r_n=<n|T|0>/<n|O_H|0>=c_H+b dot R_n, with R_I,n=<n|X_I|0>/<n|O_H|0>.
theoremCandidate.differenceIdentity: For two physical state classes n,m, Delta r_nm=b dot (R_n-R_m). The mass/improvement shear c_H cancels.
theoremCandidate.mixingCovariance: Under an invertible anomaly-operator basis change X'=A X, R'=A R and b'=A^{-T}b, so every b dot R_n and Delta r_nm is invariant.
theoremCandidate.fixedPointNull: If all anomaly coefficients vanish and the explicit-mass coefficient is common, every projective difference Delta r_nm vanishes.

oldFormulaDisposition.validSpecialCase: The D-03 Q=beta_lambda/(lambda sum D_i) is recovered only when the gauge-anomaly response difference and every other anomaly-operator response difference vanish in the chosen physical state comparison.
oldFormulaDisposition.genericCompletion: Q_full=(beta_e/2e) Delta R_F2 + beta_lambda Delta R_lambda + sum_other b_I Delta R_I.
oldFormulaDisposition.conclusion: BRST completion does not protect the quartic-only formula. It protects the cohomological beta-vector contraction; omitted gauge-sector form factors generically correct Q.
